record.original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let n > 1, and let k[n] = k[x1, ..., xn]. Given two locally nilpotent derivations P and Q of k[n], when is the smallest closed subgroup of Aut_k k[n] that contains the one-parameter subgroups {exp(tP) | t in k} and {exp(tQ) | t in k} finite-dimensional?

evidence.quote: Let P and Q be locally nilpotent derivations of k[n].
Problem 3.1. When is the minimal closed subgroup of Aut_k k[n] containing the one-dimensional subgroups {exp tP | t in k} and {exp tQ | t in k} finite dimensional?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $n > 1$ be an integer, and let $k^{[n]} = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ denote the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $k$. A $k$-derivation $D$ of $k^{[n]}$ is called locally nilpotent if for every $f \in k^{[n]}$ there exists $m \geq 1$ such that $D^m(f) = 0$. For such a $D$, the exponential
$$\exp(tD) = \sum_{i \geq 0} \frac{t^i}{i!} D^i, \qquad t \in k,$$
is a well-defined $k$-algebra automorphism of $k^{[n]}$, and $\{\exp(tD) \mid t \in k\}$ is a one-parameter subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}_k k^{[n]}$ isomorphic to the additive group $\mathbb{G}_a$. Equip $\operatorname{Aut}_k k^{[n]}$ with its standard ind-group structure, so that one can speak of closed subgroups and their dimension.

Given two locally nilpotent $k$-derivations $P$ and $Q$ of $k^{[n]}$, let $G(P,Q)$ denote the smallest closed subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}_k k^{[n]}$ that contains both one-parameter subgroups $\{\exp(tP) \mid t \in k\}$ and $\{\exp(tQ) \mid t \in k\}$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(P, Q)$ under which $G(P, Q)$ is finite-dimensional.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a problem session on affine algebraic geometry. No published solution or general criterion characterizing pairs of locally nilpotent derivations whose generated closed subgroup of automorphisms is finite-dimensional was located. Standard references on locally nilpotent derivations and ind-group structures on polynomial automorphism groups discuss related notions but do not resolve this question.

status_evidence.title: Locally nilpotent derivation - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Giving a locally nilpotent derivation on an integral domain finitely generated over a field of characteristic zero is equivalent to giving an action of the additive group Ga.
status_evidence.claim: Background confirming the link between LNDs and Ga-actions but giving no criterion for the problem.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Theory of Locally Nilpotent Derivations
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference monograph on locally nilpotent derivations.
status_evidence.claim: No general characterization for finite-dimensionality of the closed subgroup generated by two LND-induced one-parameter subgroups is given.
